sun_at — DRIVE env op

• Data kinds: any × scalar × scalar → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.sun_at(when, lat: 'float', lon: 'float', *, refraction: 'bool' = True) -> 'Dict[str, float]' (to call the implementation directly, import driveenv; driveenv.sun_at(when, lat: 'float', lon: 'float', *, refraction: 'bool' = True) -> 'Dict[str, float]'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("sun_at"))

Usage

Solar altitude and azimuth for a date/time (a timezone-aware datetime or a Julian day). The formulas are taken as is from geocam.sun_position (NOAA solar position equations = low-precision version of Meeus "Astronomical Algorithms" Chapter 25, NOAA refraction), adding the date/time handling and the Earth–Sun distance.

Returns

dict : elevation (degrees; with refraction, the apparent elevation including atmospheric refraction), elevation_geometric, azimuth (degrees clockwise from north),

declination, eq_time (equation of time, minutes), hour_angle (degrees), jd, distance_au, semidiameter (degrees).

The accuracy NOAA states is within 1 minute for sunrise/sunset times within ±72° latitude (years 1800 to 2100).

Raises ValueError: naive datetime, latitude/longitude out of range.
